title: Corgi Ventures Into Banking With AI-Powered National Charter
summary: AI-driven fintech firm Corgi files for national bank charter with OCC and FDIC, targeting small business owners with technology-enabled banking services.
body_markdown:
**Officially launched on November 17, 2026.**


#### 💡 TL;DR


- Corgi filed for a national bank charter on November 17, 2026, planning $75 million in initial capital for full-service banking operations.
- The AI-powered fintech targets its 300,000 insurance customers, mostly small business owners, with checking, savings, credit cards, and loans.
- Founded in 2024 and valued at $7 billion, Corgi leverages AI to reduce paperwork and costs across insurance, ETFs, and now banking.


AI-driven financial technology firm Corgi has officially entered the banking sector, filing applications with federal regulators on November 17, 2026 for a national bank charter and deposit insurance. The move marks the latest expansion for the San Francisco-based company, which has rapidly diversified from its 2024 insurance origins into exchange-traded funds and now full-service banking operations.


## Charter Applications and Regulatory Path


Corgi submitted its application to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency for a national bank charter alongside a parallel filing with the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation for deposit insurance. If approved, Corgi Bank, N.A. would establish its headquarters in Salt Lake City, Utah, with initial branch locations planned for San Francisco and New York.


The company selected a national charter over state-level alternatives to enable product availability across all 50 states, despite the higher regulatory and compliance costs associated with federal oversight. Jason Wessling, former president and CEO of Pacific West Bank, will serve as the proposed president of Corgi Bank.


## Release Date and Current Status


The banking charter applications were officially filed on November 17, 2026. Corgi is pursuing approval during a period when the Trump administration has prioritized accelerating new bank charter applications through the OCC, the agency that oversees banking giants including JPMorgan Chase and Wells Fargo.


## AI-Powered Banking Technology


Corgi plans to differentiate itself from traditional banks through technology-enabled services that leverage artificial intelligence to streamline operations. According to CEO Nicolas Laqua, AI enables the company to eliminate paperwork-intensive processes that were previously unavoidable, reducing costs across both banking and insurance products.


The planned banking services include checking and savings accounts, treasury services, credit cards, loans, and lines of credit. Corgi commits at least $75 million in initial capital to build the full-service banking operation, targeting the approximately 300,000 insurance customers already on its platform, most of whom are small business owners.


## Company Growth and Valuation


Founded in 2024 as an AI-powered insurance firm, Corgi has achieved a valuation of roughly $7 billion with approximately 450 employees. The company recently expanded into exchange-traded funds before pursuing the banking charter. Backed by Y Combinator, the startup incubator behind DoorDash, Airbnb, and Coinbase, Corgi raised around $450 million in its most recent funding round.


The push into banking reflects strategic demand from Corgi's existing customer base of small business owners who already rely on the company for insurance products. By offering integrated financial services under a single technology platform, Corgi aims to capture a larger share of its customers' financial relationships.


## What This Means


Corgi's banking application represents a significant test case for AI-driven financial services entering traditional regulated sectors. If approved, the company will compete directly with established banks while leveraging technology advantages that promise lower costs and faster service. For small business owners seeking streamlined financial services across insurance, investing, and banking, Corgi's integrated platform could reshape expectations for fintech convenience and affordability in the years ahead.
